quiz.0.question: Why does Italy emphasise seasonal eating (Stagionalità)?
quiz.0.options.0: For economic reasons — seasonal produce is cheaper
quiz.0.options.1: Because seasonal ingredients are at their peak flavour, and Italian food culture is built around celebrating this freshness
quiz.0.options.3: Because imported produce is not available
quiz.0.explanation: Stagionalità (seasonality) is fundamental to Italian culinary identity — using ingredients at their natural peak not only maximises flavour but connects the meal to the land and the season.
quiz.1.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical Italian summer Rosato (rosé) recommendation?
quiz.1.explanation: Amarone della Valpolicella is a powerful, full-bodied red wine (minimum 17% alcohol) — the opposite of a light summer rosé. The other three are classic Italian summer rosés.
quiz.2.question: What is the white truffle (Tartufo Bianco) season, and what is the ideal wine pairing?
quiz.2.options.1: Autumn (October–December) — aged Barolo, Barbaresco or aged white Burgundy
quiz.2.explanation: White truffles (from Alba in Piemonte) are harvested October–December. Their extraordinary earthy, musky, garlicky intensity requires the complexity of aged Barolo, Barbaresco or equivalent greatness.
quiz.3.question: On what date is Vino Novello (new wine) released in Italy?
quiz.3.explanation: Italian Vino Novello is released on 6 November — slightly later than Beaujolais Nouveau (third Thursday of November). Made by carbonic maceration, it is light, fruity and meant to be drunk immediately.
